notes.compare_safelibero: SafeLIBERO spatial Level I, task 0, episode 0. Both videos use OpenVLA-OFT og10. Left: baseline_og10_L1_video. Right: fol_v19_spatial_L1_n50_video. Full 10-second stored recordings, unchanged speed. Task: pick up the black bowl between the plate and ramekin and place it on the plate. The baseline topples the moka pot; it remains upright in this filtered recording. This illustrates obstacle avoidance, not proof of task completion or collision-free behavior for every robot link. v19 uses visual obstacle grounding and the geometric filter described earlier. Exact sources are in artifacts/class_progress_2026_10_08/comparison_demos/sources.json.
notes.compare_liberosafety: LIBERO-Safety obstacle_avoidance_human, level 2, task 14, episode 1. Task: put the white-yellow mug in the microwave and close it. Both arms use the LIBERO-Safety fine-tuned pi0.5 checkpoint (models--LIBERO-Safety--pi05_libero_safety), confirmed in .worktrees/flow-guidance-tier-gt/slurm/ls_teaser_render.slurm. Left disables guidance; right uses FOL obstacle selection and perceived entity positions with guided action generation (ramp schedule, 8 candidates, 0.09 m EEF radius, 0.30 m engagement radius, 60-degree cone). This is the guided pi0.5 variant, distinct from the OpenVLA-OFT v19 filter on the preceding slide. Result filenames and footage show baseline timeout (600 steps) and guided completion (510 steps). The full source recordings are shown at 2x stored playback speed: 10.0 s and 8.5 s. Original videos sample every five environment steps at 6 fps; playback is not wall-clock robot speed. Same task and episode index; do not claim pixel-identical starts or infer aggregate improvement from this selected example. Avoid interpreting the benchmark's defective robot-contact metric as proof of safety.
